documents.title: Optional Guidelines for AI Use in Courses
documents.stance_why: The page says faculty 'may select from among four different permission levels' and that the guidelines 'do not constitute official university policy'. It sets no single rule and hands the choice to instructors, so delegates, with the four options listed as tiers.
documents.summary: Provost-hosted optional guidelines giving instructors a four-level menu of AI permissions with ready-to-paste syllabus language, a menu of allowable-use categories, a list of unacceptable uses and a required AI Contributions disclosure. It states it is guidelines only, not official policy.

units.why: The page calls itself a shared vocabulary for AI use in 'any course context' and links to the Academic Integrity Policy; this sets scope and purpose, so it is an institution-level framework (P56) addressed to all, informing rather than commanding.
units.anchor: a shared vocabulary for when/how AI may be used in any course context
units.frag_start: These guidelines give instructors and students

units.why: The guidelines 'complement' the Academic Integrity Policy and department or college policies, which states how this framework sits within other rules; scope and framework, P56.
units.anchor: complements the Academic Integrity Policy
units.policy: The guidelines complement the Academic Integrity Policy and any department- or college-specific policies.
units.resolution_why: Only coder B found this. The source says 'This complements the Academic Integrity Policy ... as well as any department- or college-specific policies', a real statement of how the guidelines relate to other policy, so I kept it.

units.why: States the guidelines are 'guidelines only' and 'do not constitute official university policy'; this is a scope statement about the document's own status, so I place it under the institution-wide framework type (P56) as informs.

units.frag_start: The recommendations here are guidelines only
units.resolution_why: Coder A: actor all. Coder B: actor admin. The sentence tells every reader that the guidelines are not official policy, so it is addressed to all, not to an admin audience. The anchor states the rule, so policy is null.

'Instructors are invited to select and integrate the items' states a procedure and leaves the choice to instructors, so neutral. The anchor carries the rule, so policy is null.

notes: Reconciled from coder A and coder B. All five documents are university-layer pages (Provost optional guidelines, Biggio syllabus language, three Academic Integrity Office pages); no school, computing or course layer coded (course deferred). The Academic Integrity Policy PDF was not read. The Provost page and the Biggio page share sample syllabus text; each document was coded on its own. Biggio labels Option 3A 'Discourage AI use', but its text is a ban, so it is coded P01. The students' integrity page also says 'Make sure that you follow the guidance given by instructor either orally or in writing in the syllabus', which neither coder coded.
